subject.title: Native Anthropic path: replaying historical `thinking` blocks bricks long tool-use threads (`Invalid signature in thinking block` 400)

question: Which canonical fix path should own completed-turn Anthropic signed-thinking replay for non-Fable Claude models: the scoped request-builder path, the broader session-history sanitizer path, or recovery-only mitigation?
rationale: Current main still has the bug, but the open PRs change different layers with different compatibility risk around active tool-turn continuation, Fable replay, and transcript repair.

options.title: Land scoped replay-policy fix
options.body: Use the request-builder approach from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 as the canonical prevention layer, then keep recovery-carrier PRs as complementary hardening.

options.title: Adopt broad sanitizer fix
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100149 to strip non-latest signatures earlier in session history, accepting broader session-state blast radius after proof and review.

options.title: Defer prevention, land recovery only
options.body: Prioritize recovery-carrier PRs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94649 and leave completed-turn replay policy unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Land scoped replay-policy fix
recommendation.body: Use the request-builder approach from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 as the canonical prevention layer, then keep recovery-carrier PRs as complementary hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the active-tool-turn preservation rule that the canonical fix must preserve or deliberately revise.
